title: Reporting Duties to Adjusters and Employers Under a Workers' Compensation Referral
content:
# Reporting duties

Under a Workers' Compensation Referral the clinic reports to the adjuster, or to the employer for an employer direct program, on the program's timetable.

| Report | When it is due |
|---|---|
| Initial evaluation report (or the FCE report) | within the program's initial-report period in business days |
| Progress report | at least every progress-report interval in calendar days while treatment continues |
| Work status update | after every program day, where the program requires a work status update after every program day |
| Discharge report | within the program's discharge-report period in calendar days after discharge |
| Late cancellation or no-show | reported within the program's missed-visit reporting period in business days |

**Copies.** Every report is copied to the nurse case manager where the program copies reports to the nurse case manager assigned on the claim.

**No missed-visit fee to the worker.** No late-cancellation or no-show fee is charged to the worker while the program does not allow a missed-visit fee to be charged to the injured worker.

**Work status on file.** The work status on file changes only on the treating physician's written restrictions, never on the worker's or the employer's say-so.

## Points of judgement

**The employer calls to say the worker is back on full duty.** The work status on file does not change on the employer's say-so; it changes only on the treating physician's written restrictions.

**The worker says the physician has cleared them, but no written restrictions have been received.** The work status on file does not change on the worker's say-so.

**Progress reports in a program with a progress-report interval of, hypothetically, 14 days.** While treatment continues, no more than 14 calendar days pass between one progress report and the next.
